title: Migration header comment still describes round-1 behavior: erasure 'removes the row' and token 'minted lazily' contradict the round-2 tombstone + mint-at-save model documented in the same file
evidence:
--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.
--
-- continue_token is 288 bits of URL-safe entropy (wisp.random_string(48)),
-- same capability model as application.erasure_token: the token IS the
-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
-- the first "email me a link" request).

vs. the same file's column comment:
-- Erasure tombstone: a confirmed Art. 17 deletion wipes fields/token but
-- keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close ...

and upsert_application_draft.sql: 'The continue token is minted at SAVE time (COALESCE keeps an existing one) ... (W1).'
detail: Round-2 fixes changed erasure to a tombstone (erased_at, row kept — per this file's own erased_at comment) and W1 moved token minting to save time, so most rows will NOT have NULL tokens. The header block was not updated and now contradicts the schema it documents.
recommended_fix: Update the header comment: erasure tombstones the row (fields/token wiped, erased_at set, key kept until vacancy close); token minted at first save, not lazily on the first link request.
